title: Canonical tensor and unit transport maps for exceptional coefficient comparison
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings in the coefficient universe, $\varphi:A\to B$ a unital ring homomorphism, and $T$ a scheme. Work in the ordinary small-etale derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with scalar extension $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the canonical derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Write $F_T$ for ordinary sheafified scalar extension, $\mathsf Q_A,\mathsf Q_B$ for cochain localization, and $r_P:S_T\mathsf Q_AP\to\mathsf Q_B(F_TP)$ for the derived scalar counit on a cochain representative. Define the tensor normalization of a natural isomorphism $\delta:S_T(-\otimes_A^L-)\cong S_T(-)\otimes_B^LS_T(-)$ by the equations, for every cochain pair $P,Q$,
$$\delta_{\mathsf Q_AP,\mathsf Q_AQ};(r_P\otimes r_Q);\mu_B(F_TP,F_TQ)=S_T(\mu_A(P,Q));r_{P\otimes Q};\mathsf Q_B(\delta^{F_T}_{P,Q}).$$
Here semicolons mean first the left arrow then the right arrow, $\mu$ is the localization tensor comparison, and $\delta^{F_T}$ is ordinary scalar balancing. Define the unit normalization of $e:S_T\mathbf1_A\cong\mathbf1_B$ by
$$S_T(\epsilon_A);r_{\mathbf1};\mathsf Q_B(\eta^{F_T})=e;\epsilon_B,$$
where $\epsilon$ is the localization unit comparison and $\eta^{F_T}$ is the ordinary scalar unit. The predicates $\operatorname{TensorNormalizationAux}$ and $\operatorname{UnitNormalizationAux}$ are these same formulas for an additive oplax monoidal left adjoint $F:C\to D$ between Grothendieck abelian braided monoidal closed categories with monoidal preadditive structures, functorial flat resolutions and derived categories, a derived functor $E:D(C)\to D(D)$, and representative arrows $r_P:E\mathsf Q_CP\to\mathsf Q_D(FP)$. The predicates $\operatorname{TensorNormalization}$ and $\operatorname{UnitNormalization}$ are their small-etale scalar specializations. Let $\operatorname{tensorIso}$ be the isomorphism for the site's derived-tensor bifunctor uniquely equal, with its endpoints, to the unique tensor-normalized isomorphism; let $\operatorname{unitIso}$ be the unique unit-normalized isomorphism.

When $A,B$ are finite, let $f:X\to Y$ have a chosen compactification, put $G_A=Rf_A^!$, $G_B=Rf_B^!$, and $\omega_{f,A}=G_AA_Y$, $\omega_{f,B}=G_BB_Y$. Use the exceptional coefficient mate $b_{f,K}$ of [def-per-exceptional-coefficient-maps] and $c_f:Lf_B^*S_Y\cong S_XLf_A^*$ of [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso]. Define
$$\operatorname{tensorDomainMap}_{\varphi,f,K}:S_X(Lf_A^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{tensorIso}}S_XLf_A^*K\otimes_B^LS_X\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{c_f^{-1}\otimes(b_{f,A_Y};G_B(\operatorname{unitIso}_Y))}Lf_B^*S_YK\otimes_B^L\omega_{f,B}.$$
Finally define $\operatorname{TensorCompatibility}(\varphi,f,K)$ to be the equation
$$S_X(\theta_{f,A,K});b_{f,K}=\operatorname{tensorDomainMap}_{\varphi,f,K};\theta_{f,B,S_YK},$$
where $\theta$ is the canonical inverse-projection/counit tensor mate of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. This names the equation; it asserts neither its truth nor invertibility of $b$.

proof.text: For tensorIso_existsUnique use the already proved etaleHomTensorComparison_existsUnique, whose binary comparison is natural and normalized on flat-term K-flat pairs. Package its inverses as a natural isomorphism on the product category. The scalar cochain representatives are a natural transformation: apply the scalar derived adjunction to the ordinary cochain unit followed by the exact-restriction localization comparison. For arbitrary cochain P,Q choose flat-term K-flat resolutions Pprime -> P and Qprime -> Q. The two sides of TensorNormalizationAux are components of natural transformations of cochain pairs. The source maps of these resolutions are invertible after localization and derived tensor. Cancel their composite and use the known normalization at Pprime,Qprime. Uniqueness follows by restricting any all-complex-normalized comparison to the flat-term K-flat pairs and invoking the existing binary uniqueness theorem.

For siteTensorIso_existsUnique the new generic SiteTensorNormalizationAux is exactly TensorNormalizationAux on small-etale sheaves, with derivedTensor constants in its argument type. TensorNormalization specializes this generic predicate. Thus the normalized chosen isomorphism has literally the site tensor type: use reflexive heterogeneous equality for existence and eq_of_heq for uniqueness. This representation avoids repeated comparison of nested sheafification proofs; the all-complex normalization equation and the canonical comparison are unchanged.

For unitIso_existsUnique the unit complex is K-flat, so the scalar cochain representative is invertible by the exact-right-adjoint K-flat representative theorem. Ordinary scalar extension preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms because, after faithful exact restriction, it is tensoring with the constant coefficient sheaf; tensoring an acyclic K-flat complex is acyclic. The localization unit comparison is invertible, as is ordinary scalar extension of the unit. Compose these three isomorphisms and the inverse target localization unit comparison. Its hom satisfies UnitNormalizationAux by cancellation, and cancellation also proves uniqueness.

proof_origin.place: B3 proves the tensor, site tensor transport and unit normalization auxiliary theorems by the recorded arguments. The main exceptional_coefficient_comparison theorem and its ten-step plan remain unchanged, as does the previously proved compactSupportMap_isIso.

lean.statement:
def tensorDomainMap [Finite A] [Finite B] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] (K : DerivedCategoryModule A Y) :
    (scalarExtension φ X).obj
      (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj
        ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).leftDerivedFunctor.obj K)).obj
          (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f)) ⟶
    ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) X).obj
      ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f).leftDerivedFunctor.obj
        ((scalarExtension φ Y).obj K))).obj (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f)
